uncited: Rendering Strategy and Optimization is a family of techniques that accelerate volume rendering by optimizing the efficiency of ray-grid traversal and determining optimal data structures for a given scene [15795-optimization-and-cost-models.md].
It addresses the computational bottleneck of evaluating every voxel or primitive along a ray, which is often redundant due to empty space or coarse sampling [15795-optimization-and-cost-models.md].

Unlike sibling methods that define specific traversal algorithms (e.g., [Digital Differential Analyzer (DDA) Traversal](3061-digital-differential-analyzer-dda-traversal.md), [Octree and Tree Traversal](4134-octree-and-tree-traversal.md)), this family focuses on *how* to execute traversal more efficiently (via hardware awareness or algorithmic shortcuts) and *what* resolution to use (via cost models) to minimize total rendering time [15795-optimization-and-cost-models.md].
All methods in this family build on [Ray-grid traversal](17-ray-grid-traversal.md), which advances analytically from one cell boundary to the next .
The core mechanism determines the next cell by comparing distances to upcoming boundaries on the x, y, and z axes, selecting the minimum distance to advance .

Optimization and cost models do not alter this fundamental geometric logic but instead optimize the *cost* of executing it or the *parameters* (like grid resolution) under which it runs [15795-optimization-and-cost-models.md].
